job.title: Senior Financial Accountant
job.description:
This is a rare opportunity to join a highly successful private enterprise which develops and manages a diverse portfolio of residential housing and community development projects across Australia. The business is managed by a highly experienced leadership team and maintains a values-driven, collaborative and down-to-earth workplace culture.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, and as part of a small finance team, this broadly scoped role is primarily responsible for managing the periodic financial reporting, project accounting and all taxation compliance requirements for all entities within the Group. You will use your strong technical accounting skills to prepare accurate and timely monthly management reports, monitor and analyse cashflow and variances to budgets and forecasts and provide insightful analytical commentary to support operational decision making and business planning. You will be responsible for the preparation and lodgement of the annual income tax returns for all entities in the Group, and your detailed understanding of Australian Taxation compliance principles will be invaluable in ensuring that the enterprise continues to meet its periodic Indirect and Direct taxation compliance obligations. Additionally, you will help to coordinate the Group’s external accountants, tax advisors and auditors through the year end audit process and you will be expected to form collaborative working relationships with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders.

This is a broadly scoped and highly engaging role for a career minded CA/CPA qualified accounting professional now seeking the next step in their professional services career. You should possess demonstrable financial accounting expertise combined with a strong technical understanding of relevant Australian accounting and taxation principles, either gained in a Business Services & Tax environment or perhaps in a similar role in industry. Prior exposure to, or experience in, the property development sector is highly desirable. Previous experience with MYOB Advanced will also be well regarded.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact James McBeath on 0438 825 651.  Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.

job.title: Security Coordinator
job.description:
South Bank Corporation is the renowned place manager behind Brisbane's premier recreational, cultural, educational and entertainment precinct, South Bank. With a vision to be a world-leading urban precinct that welcomes, engages and inspires, we are committed to innovating, managing and maintaining our enviable reputation while recognising the growing demand for green space in Brisbane's inner city.

The South Bank precinct spans 42 hectares, including 1.2 km of tree-lined riverfront and over 14 hectares of parkland, attracts 16.6 million people a year, hosts hundreds of events activities, supports over 9500 jobs and contributes over $2.4 billion to the Queensland economy.  

As Brisbane prepares to host Brisbane 2032, South Bank Corporation plays a pivotal role in ensuring our iconic precinct is ready to showcase Brisbane and Queensland on the world stage.

This key role as Security Coordinator is responsible for supporting security arrangements across protective, physical, and personnel security initiatives. You will work closely with the Security Manager and Security Supervisor to assist with public safety and facilities protection, whilst supporting customer experience, events, operations, and major contractors. 

As Security Coordinator, you will be responsible for the following;

  • Coordinating day-to-day physical security arrangements including access control, CCTV, keys, building security, and perimeter security, to ensure security is not compromised.
  • Coordinating the development of a Security Operations Manual and reviewing documentation and protocols, including a focus on at-risk people and customer-centric security arrangements. 
  • Contribute to the development, review, and continuous improvement of security policies, procedures, and standard operating guidelines.
  • Support protective security arrangements to ensure standards and expectations are met and collaborating closely with contractors to address issues.
  • Identifying security trends and issues from local, national, and international perspectives and escalating risks and concerns via Intelligence Bulletins and Security Briefs.
  • Assisting with incident investigations, including footage reviews, causal analysis, and developing mitigations, reports, and debriefs to close out incidents.
  • Supporting events via the preparation of Security Briefs and general event security planning to present for approval and endorsement
  • Preparing a security audit schedule and conducting audits on facilities and functions with internal stakeholders and presenting results for approval. 
  • Supporting customer experience teams and incident rooms during major events.
  • Liaison with internal and external stakeholders to support the overall security arrangements.
  • Participating in internal and external security precinct training exercises and coordinating forums, including logistical arrangements and preparation and circulation of minutes and debriefs.
  • Ensuring compliance with Australia’s Strategy for Protecting Crowded Places from Terrorism and relevant legislation. 
  • Supporting security culture and awareness campaigns.


Key Skills & Experience Required

  • Tertiary qualifications in criminology, justice studies, and/or intelligence are highly desirable.
  • Work experience as a security or intelligence professional in a similar environment with strategic and operational responsibilities is highly desirable
  • Working knowledge of crowded places security obligations and requirements, including Australia’s Strategy for Protecting Crowded Places from Terrorism.
  • Experience in developing procedures and protocols. 
  • Sound understanding of precinct security risks and threats.
  • Highly developed analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving skills and the ability to develop insights, identify trends and emerging issues, and communicate and disseminate advice.
  • Excellent liaison and negotiation skills demonstrated via experience dealing with law enforcement agencies and internal and external stakeholders from the Government, private sector, and community. 
  • Excellent oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • High level of integrity and professionalism demonstrated by experience in sensitive environments.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of physical and protective security systems relating to access control and surveillance, combined with a strong record of achievement.
  • This role may be required to work outside of normal business hours, including weekends.


If this sounds like your next career step, please contact Ian Quinn on 0403 343 097 for a strictly confidential discussion.  Alternatively, submit your application via the Apply button.

Closing date for applications is midnight 16 October 2026.
